pairs.subject: review-iteration-loops
pairs.evidence: lib/script/trailer/plan.ts:27 The trailer revision engine's output schema is only {ops, summary}, with no refusals field (the sibling lib/script/editPlan.ts:42 has one). So the model cannot refuse a note with a reason, and the only refusal is the validator rejecting the whole plan, not the engine declining a note.

techniques.evidence: lib/script/trailer/plan.ts:27 Refusing an invalid plan before it is applied is right (parseTrailerPlan runs before the replay), but refusal is not a first-class engine output next to the ops, and there is no explicitly-unchanged list.

lib/script/trailer/plan.ts:157 The plan is a list of per-beat patches replayed over the saved cut, so beats no op names stay untouched. It is all-or-nothing (line 106), and the saved cut does not change until the creator accepts.
lib/script/trailer/notes.ts:3 Each violation becomes a typed suggested note carrying the finding's sentence, located by beat. Unmeasured rows propose nothing.

lib/script/trailer/notes.ts:15 A closed vocabulary (fix-connector, collapse-raises, name-payer, hold-asset) plus a custom hatch, each kind named for its repair. Its registers are rule repairs rather than focus/scope/order.
lib/script/trailer/plan.ts:131 The spine (kind, movement) the creator confirmed in Step 1 beats any model plan: a patch that touches it is refused and the governing decision is named.
lib/script/trailer/plan.ts:42 Patchable fields are text only (label, text, connector, raises, spends). Discrete media have no acoustic or visual seam.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Document.tsx:78 The focus/scope/order kinds are offered per card (NoteKind = more-focus|less-focus|descope|move-earlier|move-later|custom), but custom is filtered out, so there is no honest free-text hatch.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Document.tsx:204 A staged recalibration shows its refusals verbatim next to accept and discard. The refusal guards run before apply in lib/script/recalibrate.ts.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Document.tsx:196 The revised version is staged and gated again before it can be accepted. Accepting over a blocking gate is a separate, recorded act.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Document.tsx:189 A candidate that still speaks material descoped in Research is shown as a conflict with the scope decision (scopeConflicts). The refusal guard is recalibrate.ts GUARD 1.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Notebook.tsx:147 Follow-up results list typed effects, each applied or rejected one at a time (line 151). The effect vocabulary includes 'kills' and 'downgrades' (lib/research/followup.ts:22), and 'unanswered' is a terminal status.
lib/script/impact.ts:100 The coverage and spend views in Document.tsx draw per-card seconds produced by this largest-remainder split, which sums exactly to the beat.

pairs.subject: review-iteration-loops
pairs.evidence: lib/producers/scoutPieceActs.ts:197 A piece reuses the kept trial clips by reference and re-makes only the rejected panels, then records the concatenated cut straight away. Nothing gates the joins between kept and re-made clips (no level match, no continuity check), so per-clip approval stands in for a verdict on the whole piece.

techniques.evidence: lib/producers/scoutPieceActs.ts:197 Kept clips are held by reference (line 152, reusedOf checks the priced path), and re-made clips get a new seed (scoutPiece.ts:97). cutArgs only normalises stream shape, with no loudness match and no seam gate before the piece is booked.

lib/producers/scoutReelActs.ts:291 Lint findings (each rule phrased as the requirement, with a line excerpt) go to the automated fix turn along with the current page, and the strip is linted again after the fix (line 297). A strip still failing lint fails the reel.

pairs.subject: review-iteration-loops
pairs.evidence: lib/decision/v1/sources/scout.ts:90 Committing a scout night writes every verdict, reason and note into night.json in the night's own media folder, last and idempotently. No rejected or unchosen media is destroyed in the same operation, and the record never says what is gone, so judgement and bytes stay stored together.

techniques.evidence: lib/decision/v1/sources/scout.ts:90 The record half is sound: rejects carry reasons (line 399), and committed is written last, so the record works as a queue of completed writes (line 91). The destruction half is missing: no prune of rejected media, no 'gone' entry, no rule that only one frame per approval is kept.

pairs.registryProposal: gate-record-outlives-the-media assumes generation and review run on different machines. Where both run on one box and rejected media feeds later taste learning, the standard should say whether destroying it is still required or only recommended.
